1. (Currently amended) A gas generator comprising: a composition containing an alkali metal chlorate as an oxidizer provided at about 25-75 weight percent, and a carboxylic acid as a fuel provided at about 25-75 weight percent, said percentages stated by weight of the total composition; and a desiccant in operable communication with said composition, wherein said desiccant is selected from activated calcium sulfate, silica, zeolite, clay, and calcium oxide, and is provided in an amount effective to maintain thermal stability of said composition during heat aging.

2. (Currently amended) The gas generator of claim 1 wherein said desiccant is mixed into said composition at about 10-35 weight percent of the total composition and is effective to reduce decomposition of the carboxylic acid fuel.

3. (Currently amended) The gas generator of claim 1 wherein said desiccant is in vapor communication with, but physically separated from, said composition, and said desiccant is provided in amounts resulting in a mass differential of about -5.0 to 5.0% of the composition after heat aging at 107°C for 400 hours, wherein the desiccant inhibits decomposition of the fuel by adsorbing decomposition products.

4. (Currently amended) The gas generator of claim 1 wherein said composition contains an extrusion aid provided at about 0.1-10 weight percent of the total gas generant composition, and wherein said extrusion aid is selected from graphite, fumed silica, and mixtures thereof.

5. (Previously presented) The gas generator of claim 4 wherein said extrusion aid is selected from graphite, fumed silica, and mixtures thereof.

6. (Previously presented) The gas generator of claim 1 wherein said alkali metal chlorate is potassium chlorate.

7. (Previously presented) The gas generator of claim 1 wherein said carboxylic acid is selected from tartaric acid and its isomers, succinic acid, glutamic acid, adipic acid, and mucic acid, and mixtures thereof.

8. (Currently amended) The gas generator of claim 1 wherein said carboxylic acid is DL-tartaric acid, and wherein the use of DL-tartaric acid provides enhanced thermal stability compared to individual enantiomers due to increased lattice energy in the racemic crystals.

9. (Currently amended) A gas generating system comprising: a gas generator comprising a composition, said composition containing an alkali metal chlorate as an oxidizer provided at about 25-75 weight percent, and said composition further containing a carboxylic acid as a fuel provided at about 25-75 weight percent, said percentages stated by weight of the total gas generant composition; and a desiccant in operable communication with said composition, wherein said desiccant is selected from activated calcium sulfate, silica, zeolite, clay, and calcium oxide, and is provided in an amount effective to maintain thermal stability of said composition.

10. (Currently amended) The gas generating system of claim 9 wherein said desiccant is mixed into said composition at about 10-35 weight percent of the total composition and is effective to reduce decomposition of the carboxylic acid fuel.

11. (Currently amended) The gas generating system of claim 9 wherein said desiccant is in vapor communication with, but physically separated from, said composition, and wherein the desiccant inhibits decomposition of the fuel by adsorbing decomposition products.

12. (Previously presented) The gas generating system of claim 9 wherein said system is a vehicle occupant protection system.

13. (Currently amended) A composition comprising: an alkali metal chlorate as an oxidizer provided at about 25-75 weight percent; a carboxylic acid as a fuel provided at about 25-75 weight percent; and a desiccant selected from activated calcium sulfate, silica, zeolite, clay, and calcium oxide, provided at about 5-35 weight percent, said percentages stated by weight of the total gas generant composition, wherein the desiccant is effective to inhibit decomposition of the fuel by adsorbing decomposition products and maintaining thermal stability.

14. (Previously presented) The composition of claim 13 wherein said carboxylic acid is selected from tartaric acid and its isomers, DL-tartaric acid, succinic acid, glutamic acid, adipic acid, and mucic acid, and mixtures thereof.

15. (Previously presented) The composition of claim 13 wherein said alkali metal chlorate is potassium chlorate.

16. (Previously presented) The composition of claim 13 wherein said desiccant is selected from activated calcium sulfate, silica, zeolite, clay, and calcium oxide.

17. (Currently amended) The composition of claim 13 wherein said desiccant is zeolite, and wherein zeolite is selected as the preferred adsorbent to inhibit fuel decomposition.

18. (Currently amended) The composition of claim 13 wherein said desiccant is selected to provide a mass differential of about -5.0% to 5.0% after heat aging at 107°C for 400 hours, wherein the desiccant inhibits decomposition of the fuel by adsorbing decomposition products.
